messages:
sarah_support: Heads up — customer 'ACME Payments' opened a ticket: sudden latency + egress spike. They claim their requests should stick to us-west but are landing in ap-south intermittently. Attaching sample logs.
raj_infra: Can you paste the failover config and a repro curl? also which API key / project id?
sarah_support: project: acme-payments, api_key: redacted. Repro (from their infra):\n```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' -v
```
logs show: `X-Served-Region: ap-south-1` even though failover policy lists us-west first.
mina_runtime: Can you paste the failover_policy JSON blob from their route? suspect parsing weirdness.
sarah_support: Here you go (copied from customer UI):\n```
"failover_policy": {
  "ordered_regions": ["2","10","11"],
  "sticky_ttl": 300
}
```
(They intended numeric priorities: 2 -> primary, then 10, then 11)
raj_infra: Aha. If ordered_regions are treated as strings and we sort lexicographically anywhere in the decision path, the effective order becomes ["10","11","2"]. That would make traffic go to the region with id 10 first. :eyes:
mina_runtime: Pushing a quick check to the runtime selector — we do a sorted() call on the region list without explicit numeric conversion in a couple of code paths. Repro steps for me: set ordered_regions to ["2","10"] and watch which region the selector picks when primary is down.
sarah_support: Customer also sent a short trace during the spike: `selector: chose region-10 due to fallback_list[0]` and increased egress to ap-south-1. Billing shows a jump for cross-region egress.
tim_oncall: Need to triage urgency. If this is our sorting bug, rollback plan? Also support refund for their cross-region egress during incident window.
raj_infra: Immediate mitigation: treat ordered_regions as ordinal numbers when all items match /^\d+$/; fallback to current behavior for opaque ids. I'll open a quick PR to coerce strings to ints before sorting. Also add a unit test for mixed numeric ids.
mina_runtime: I'll try a runtime patch to avoid any implicit global sort in the hot path (cheap guard). If we can short-circuit when there's an explicit order provided (no sorting), that's safest.
sarah_support: Customer asked for repro steps we can run from their environment. Here's a minimal repro they gave us:\n```
# primary (2) marked unhealthy in control plane
# client sends normal requests
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip}\n"; done
```
They see ~60% hits to ap-south and ~40% to us-west.
raj_infra: Thanks — I can reproduce locally with the exact blob. Confirmed the selector returns region-10 as fallback first. Will ship hotfix and a database migration to normalize stored ordered_regions to numeric array when appropriate.
tim_oncall: Please post PR/CL and ETA. Also set support escalation: Finance to hold the billing charge and mark for review.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3472. Owner: raj_infra. Priority: P2.
mina_runtime: Quick note — zero-pad is another option but fragile. Numeric coercion is better. Also adding a lint in the UI to prevent users from entering purely numeric strings (or convert in-place with a tooltip) while we patch.
sarah_support: Customer replied: thanks for fast response; would like a short statement and ETA for fix + potential credit. I told them we'll update in 2h.
raj_infra: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/selector/changes/345 (draft) — small change: if items.every(isDigits) then sort by Number(a)-Number(b) else keep original ordering. Rolling to staging now.
mina_runtime: Deployed to staging, running traffic replay. Selector now respects intended numeric order. Will run load test then prod roll.
tim_oncall: Once prod fix is live, run backfill to compute misrouted request count for ACME and approve credit. Keep me posted.
sarah_support: thx team. I'll update customer and mark incident INC-2026-3472 as ongoing. :thumbsup:
